Composite-Weight Stability Under Case Resampling

Source: R/mcml_pc.R
loading_stability.Rd

loading_stability() bootstraps the item weights of a build_mcml_pc() fit and returns a pc_loading_stability object with each item's observed signed weight, its bootstrap mean and standard deviation, a percentile interval and how often its sign flipped. Each replicate resamples the rows of the raw data with replacement, re-estimates the node-level network with the fit's estimator (cor, pcor or glasso; any other node-level method is re-estimated as cor) and correlation type, and reapplies the fitted weighting scheme, data-dependent and custom weights and the factor-analysis options included. A fit with a descriptive aggregation ("average", "escoufier", "cancor") has its item-table weights, the "strength" weights, resampled. Experimental.

Wide intervals mean the weighting should not be over-interpreted. Equal weights keep their magnitudes in every replicate, so for them only the sign flips carry information; a sign that flips often marks an item whose reverse-keying is not settled by the data. Supplied numeric weights are fixed in magnitude and sign, so their intervals have zero width and resampling them tells nothing. The intervals describe the weights, not the macro network: edge-weight intervals for it come from bootstrap_network() on its macro network.

Usage

loading_stability(x, iter = 200L, ci_level = 0.05, seed = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'pc_loading_stability'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'pc_loading_stability'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'pc_loading_stability'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An mcml_pc object that carries its raw data; one built from a network without data raises an error, and so does an older saved fit with custom weights, which must be rebuilt with build_mcml_pc() to keep its weighting. For the print() and plot() methods: a pc_loading_stability object.

iter

The number of bootstrap replicates, at least 2. Default 200; each replicate re-estimates the node-level network, so this is slower than a plain bootstrap.

ci_level

The tail level of the percentile intervals: 0.05 (default) gives 95% intervals.

seed

An integer that makes the resampling reproducible. Default NULL. The session's own random stream is left as it was.

digits

For the print() method: the decimal places of the numeric columns. Default 3.

...

For the print(), summary() and plot() methods: ignored.

object

For the summary() method: a pc_loading_stability object.

Value

A pc_loading_stability object. print() shows the item table and summary() returns it; plot() draws each item's signed weight with its interval, one panel per cluster. The object's fields:

summary

A data frame with one row per item: node, cluster, weight (the observed signed weight), boot_mean, boot_sd, ci_lower, ci_upper and sign_flips (the share of replicates in which the item's sign differed from the observed one).

boot_weights

The iter x items matrix of resampled signed weights.

iter, ci_level

The settings used.

For the methods: print() returns x invisibly, plot() a ggplot.

For the summary() method: the item table, a data frame with one row per item and the columns listed under summary above.

Methods

  • plot() draws each item's observed signed composite weight with its bootstrap percentile interval, one panel per cluster, with a dashed line at zero.

Examples

set.seed(1)
f <- stats::rnorm(100)
g <- stats::rnorm(100)
df <- data.frame(a1 = f + stats::rnorm(100), a2 = f + stats::rnorm(100),
                 a3 = f + stats::rnorm(100), b1 = g + stats::rnorm(100),
                 b2 = g + stats::rnorm(100), b3 = g + stats::rnorm(100))
cl <- list(A = c("a1", "a2", "a3"), B = c("b1", "b2", "b3"))
fit <- build_mcml_pc(df, cl, aggregation = "loadings",
                     method = "cor")
stability <- loading_stability(fit, iter = 50, seed = 1)
stability
#> Composite-Weight Stability (case bootstrap, experimental)
#>   50 replicates | 95% percentile CIs
#> 
#>  node cluster weight boot_mean boot_sd ci_lower ci_upper sign_flips
#>    a1       A  0.338     0.332   0.021    0.292    0.370          0
#>    a2       A  0.336     0.339   0.018    0.308    0.375          0
#>    a3       A  0.326     0.329   0.021    0.290    0.367          0
#>    b1       B  0.316     0.317   0.022    0.276    0.348          0
#>    b2       B  0.350     0.346   0.022    0.310    0.393          0
#>    b3       B  0.334     0.337   0.015    0.307    0.360          0
